chapter: Trent's band: Arkansas, Dallas and the Adolphus
title: Paul Whiteman hears the band and tells them to go national
summary: Whiteman praises Mosley and the band in the press, takes them to his concert, and they listen to his and the California Ramblers' records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: YOU NEVER HEARD OF ANY OTHER, NOW WHERE DOES THE PART WITH PAUL WHITEMAN COME IN. DID WHITEMAN COME DOWN THERE.

Yeah, see we had been at the Adolphis I guess about six months and Paul Whiteman came in and that was one of the greatest moments of my life. When we came off the bandstand, he came over and he shook my hand and said you're quite a young man on that trombone. I thought that was the greatest thing. Everybody in those days looked upon Paul Whiteman almost as a god really. He said, I'm going to have the whole band come in and hear you fellows. And sure enough, that's how I met Michael F?, Ross Gorman and Henry Buzzy, all those guys. They had --it seems as just yesterday. We played in the junior ballroom, I don't know why they called it junior because it was the largest ballroom in the hotel. It was a long place, very wide and over to the right here, Paul Whiteman had his whole band. He had already arranged for them to set up a table for us. He just raved about the band, both in the press and to us.
It was. That was one of the things that really helped to sell Trent.
THEY WERE PLAYING AT THE HOTEL AT THE TIME.

They were staying. No Whiteman was only doing big concerts. He was on a concert tour. He gave us tickets. We caught his concert. We didn't care if we had to go up on a mountaintop. We wanted to hear Paul Whiteman.
WHAT KIND OF MUSIC WERE YOU GUYS LISTENING TO OTHER THAN TO WHAT YOU WERE PLAYING. WHAT KIND OF RECORDS WERE YOU LISTENING TO. WERE YOU LISTENING TO PAUL WHITEMAN RECORDS.

We were listening to Paul Whiteman's records and one of the bands that we were listening, the California Ramblers and I'll never forget they made a record on (da da da). Then they made another one on DoWakadoo. Do you remember that song and the trumpet player took a solo that it always stuck in my mind. He had a gorgeous tone and he had a beautiful style.
